name: edit_item
description:
Item-level timeline operations across types: `video` (incl. B-roll cutaways), `audio`, `image`, `gif`, `svg`, `motion-graphic`, `effect`, `transition`. Existing legacy `solid` items may be deleted, but edit_item does not create, duplicate, or update solids; use opaque Motion Graphics for title cards, backgrounds, and color mattes. Captions are not items — never create, move, or edit them here; see # Captions boundary. Pass one or more of `adds`, `updates`, `deletes`, plus optional `validateOnly` / `ripple`; the whole batch commits atomically and a single validation failure rolls everything back. Bundle related ops in one call — delete+add swap, update+add reposition, splice via `alignTo: "track-end"`, and update-swaps all work atomically.

# Safety defaults

- `validateOnly:true`: dry-run validation/planning; no commit; preview IDs are not reusable. Do not combine with `ripple:true`.
- Preserve existing timeline item positions by default. Use `ripple:true` when the edit intent clearly implies inserting into an existing sequence, making room, shifting later items, or closing gaps.
- "Add/place/move to 5s" is not by itself a ripple request. If no exact track is required, omit `trackId` so auto-placement can choose a non-overlapping track; updates first try the original track, then may move only that updated item to avoid overlap.
- If the user names an exact track and the range overlaps, do not silently move other items; ask or use `validateOnly:true` to compare new layer vs replacement vs ripple insertion.

## adds — create items

- Required: media-backed items need `type` + `assetId`; `fromItemId` duplicates an existing committed item. Do not create or duplicate `solid` items; create an opaque Motion Graphic for cards, backgrounds, and color fills.
- Apply Motion Graphics templates from `browse_library` with `manage_template action:"apply"`; their Library IDs are not project asset IDs and cannot be added through `edit_item`.
- Library Sound Effects from `browse_library` use `{type:"audio",assetId:"library:sound:<id>",fromFrame:<anchor frame>}`. For these adds only, `fromFrame` is the sound's anchor/editorial moment frame; edit_item imports/reuses the project audio asset, keeps the full audio, and shifts the actual item start so the anchor lands there.
- Library Zoom presets from `browse_library` can be added as effects with `assetId:"library:zoom:<preset>"`. edit_item expands the preset to `builtin:zoom` and applies its default shape/magnification.
- Full-screen opaque Motion Graphics own their background. Do not add a separate `solid` underneath one just to set card color; set the MG `bgColor` / `transparentBackground` properties instead.
- Asset type must match item type: audio items require audio assets. A video asset with embedded audio is still `type:"video"`; add it as video to keep embedded audio, or extract/upload a separate audio asset for independent audio-only placement.
- Position: `fromFrame` for exact frames; `from` for explicit time strings; `alignTo:"track-end"|"timeline-end"`; or `trackId` only to append on that track.
- Duration: required for `image` / `gif` / `svg`; `video` / `audio` / `motion-graphic` infer asset duration when omitted. Use `durationInFrames` for exact edits.
- Source offsets: use `sourceStartFromInSeconds` for video / audio / gif source trimming; source range must stay inside the asset. Video keeps visual + embedded audio timing together.
- Layout: visual adds may use `opacity`, `width`/`height`, anchors, `rotation`, `fit`, `crop*`, `borderRadius`, and fade fields — placement and fit rules in # Canvas placement.
- Stacking: V1 = back. Omit `trackId` for non-overlap auto-placement; this avoids same-track time overlap, not canvas overlap.
- **`fromItemId` must reference an already-committed item** — to duplicate a freshly-added item, use a second `edit_item` call after `preview_timeline`.

## updates — modify items

`{id, ...changedFields}` (id can be a short prefix from `preview_timeline`). Editable fields by category:

- Timeline guard: pass `timelineId` from `manage_timelines list` when intentionally updating an item on a specific timeline. Without it, stale item IDs from inactive timelines are rejected.
- Position: `fromFrame` / `fromDeltaFrames` / `trackId`. Omit `trackId` to preserve the current track when possible, or auto-move only this item to a non-overlapping track when the new time would collide. Pass `trackId` to require an exact track; exact-track overlap still errors.
- Timing/source: `durationInFrames`; `playbackRate` only for `audio` / `gif` / `video`; use `sourceStartFromInSeconds` to trim the start of video/audio/gif source media.
- Audio: prefer `decibelAdjustment` for exact dB changes; `0` means unchanged, `-60` is effectively silent. Compatibility aliases `volume` / `audioVolume` accept only 0–1 linear slider values (`0` silent, `1` unchanged) and `muted:true` means silent; do not pass values above 1 to those aliases. Use `audioFadeIn`, `audioFadeOut` for fades. For "duck music under voice/speech", use `edit_track` roles instead: voice/speech track `role:"anchor"`, BGM/background music track `role:"follower"`; leave `audioRouting.duckDepthDb` unset unless the user explicitly asks for more or less music under speech.
- Visual: `opacity`, size/anchors, `rotation`, `fit`, `crop*`, `borderRadius`, `fadeIn`, `fadeOut`.
- Aspect-locked: for raw manual resize, pass only one of `width`/`height`; `fit:"cover"` / `fit:"contain"` preserves aspect ratio automatically (rules in # Canvas placement).

**Immutable**: `type`, `assetId`, `fromItemId`. To swap an asset → `deletes` + `adds` in the same call. Delete+add does not automatically copy the old item's source/layout fields — read the old item and include the `fromFrame`, `durationInFrames`, `trackId`, `sourceStartFromInSeconds`, crop/layout/fades/etc. you want to preserve.

**MG `propertyOverrides`**: PATCH semantics — merges with existing. `null` per-key removes override; `propertyOverrides: null` clears all. Discover valid property keys/types with `inspect_item` and `inspect_asset` before guessing. For MG code itself, use `edit_asset`. **Caveat**: shrinking a motion-graphic outer item's `duration` truncates the baked inner animation — regenerate the MG asset for a different duration instead.

# Fades

Use native fade fields for ordinary fade-in/fade-out requests. Fade values are seconds, not frames:

- Visual opacity fades: `fadeIn`, `fadeOut`.
- Audio/video volume fades: `audioFadeIn`, `audioFadeOut`. On audio-only items, `fadeIn` / `fadeOut` are accepted as audio fades.
- Example: `audioFadeOut:1.5` means a 1.5-second audio fade-out. At 30fps, a 60-frame fade is `audioFadeOut:2` or `audioFadeOutDurationInFrames:60`; do not write `audioFadeOut:60` unless you want 60 seconds.
- Add separate media or Motion Graphic overlay/matte items only when the user explicitly asks for an independent visual layer.

## deletes — remove items

`{id}` or `{id, type}` (`type` required for `effect` / `transition`). Pass `timelineId` when deleting an item on a specific or non-active timeline.

## Multi-timeline targeting

Edits target the active timeline by default. To intentionally edit a different timeline without switching, pass that timeline's prefix/full id from `manage_timelines list` as `timelineId` on each `adds[]`, `updates[]`, or `deletes[]` entry. Track aliases like `V1` / `A1` then resolve inside that target timeline. If the item ID and `timelineId` disagree, the tool rejects the edit instead of silently mutating the wrong cut.

# When NOT to use — transcript-based editing → Script

If the requested end state changes which spoken words, sentences, transcript segments, topics, highlights, or takes play, use Script (`read_script` → `Edit timeline.md` → `apply_script`), not `edit_item`. `sourceStartFromInSeconds` is media addressing, not transcript-based speech selection.

# Captions boundary

Do not use `edit_item` for captions. Captions are not normal timeline items — a singleton timeline overlay with sources inside; do not create caption items or tracks, and do not move, trim, delete, or count captions through item operations. Use `edit_captions` (writes, incl. enable/source/style/layout/language/visibility) and `read_captions` (reads).

# Canvas placement (adds and updates)

For background/full-bleed visuals, prefer `fit:"cover"` with no manual geometry. For a crop-to-box or contain-in-box placement, combine `fit` with a target rectangle, for example `{fit:"cover", left:50, top:880, width:160, height:160}`. `fit:"cover"` / `fit:"contain"` can target the whole canvas or a manual box (`left`/`top`/`width`/`height`, or right/bottom anchors); do not combine `fit` with explicit `crop*`. Without `fit`, manual placement passes dimensions plus one horizontal anchor (`left` or `right`) and one vertical anchor (`top` or `bottom`); do not pass both sides on an axis.

# Effects, transitions

- **Effect on a clip**: `{type:"effect", targetItemId, assetId}`. `targetItemId` is the existing video/image/gif item to receive the effect; do not use `fromItemId` for effects (that field duplicates regular media items). This lands exactly like dragging the effect from the library onto the clip: a track effect in the clip's Effect lane, covering the clip's full range and following the clip when it moves. Effects do not apply to motion-graphic items.
- **Effect on a track range**: `{type:"effect", assetId:"builtin:zoom", trackId:"V1", fromFrame:120, durationInFrames:60}` or the explicit `trackBoundFrom` / `trackBoundDurationInFrames` fields. Anchors to the clip under the range start; over empty track space it becomes an adjustment-layer Effect spanning the range.
- **Layout is a track effect, not manual geometry**: add built-in layout assets with the same effect shape. Use `targetItemId` for a clip-scoped layout that affects only that clip; use an existing `trackId` + range on an empty/top Effect lane for an adjustment-layout that dynamically wraps eligible visible video/image/gif clips below it. Built-ins: `builtin:layout-screen-face-bubble`, `builtin:layout-social-screen-stack`, `builtin:layout-two-up-split`.
- **Layout examples**: clip PiP frame treatment → `{type:"effect", assetId:"builtin:layout-screen-face-bubble", targetItemId:"cameraClipId"}`; dynamic auto split screen over sources below an existing host lane → `{type:"effect", assetId:"builtin:layout-two-up-split", trackId:"V3", fromFrame:0, durationInFrames:180}`. Do not resize clips by hand unless the user asks to bake/detach a layout.
- **Layout tuning**: update the `effect-track:<id>` (from `preview_timeline`) with `propertyOverrides:{__chatcutLayout:{...}}` — PATCH-like: `params` (`bubblePosition`, `bubbleSizeRatio`, `bubbleRadiusRatio`, `gapRatio`, `paddingRatio`, `safeMarginRatio`, `fit`, `focalIntent`), `captionPlacement` (layout caption policy), `sourcePolicy.pinnedRoles` (`screen` / `camera` / `primary` / `secondary` → item ids). Panel-layout (`layout-two-up-split`, `layout-social-screen-stack`) `params.fit`: `cover` (crop, default), `contain` (fit entire image), `fit-width`; never `fill` unless the user explicitly asks to stretch/distort.
- **Screen + Face Bubble margin**: this preset intentionally defaults to a small safe margin. Do not set `paddingRatio:0` or `safeMarginRatio:0` unless the user asks for edge-to-edge bubble placement.
- **Face-tracked zoom**: for real-time face tracking, first add or find a `builtin:zoom` track effect, then call `apply_zoom_tracking` on its `effect-track:<prefix>` id. Do not fake tracking by setting `focalMode:"track"` without a real `__chatcutReframeCurve`.
- **AI reframe curve foundation**: use `assetId:"builtin:zoom"` with reserved `propertyOverrides.__chatcutReframeCurve` only when you have a versioned `ReframeCurveV1` payload (`version:1`, `timebase:"effect-frame"`, `coordinateSpace:"composition-normalized"`, sparse keyframes with `frame`, `focalPointX`, `focalPointY`, `magnification`). Do not mutate `crop*` every few frames or invent another curve shape. `magnification` accepts 0.05-16; values below 1 zoom out, ordinary UI zooms usually stay 1-4, and explicit close-up requests like 8x are allowed.
- Either way the effect IS a track effect — there is no separate per-clip effect kind. `preview_timeline` lists it under the track's effects; update/delete uses that id with `type:"effect"`.
- **LUT** (effect with `category="lut"`): same shape, `propertyOverrides: {intensity: 0–1}`. `assetId` is the LUT effect asset's own id (a built-in `builtin:` LUT, or the project asset an uploaded `.cube` created) — there is no literal `"lut"` assetId and no nested LUT binding inside `propertyOverrides`. Swap → delete + add with a different `assetId`.
- **Add/replace transition**: `{type:"transition", assetId, outgoingItemId, incomingItemId}`; boundary shorthand `{type:"transition", assetId, trackId:"V1", fromFrame:120, durationInFrames:30}` works only when endpoints are unambiguous. Built-in transition assets use `builtin:tr-*` ids (e.g. `builtin:tr-cross-dissolve`, `builtin:tr-dip-to-black`, audio cross fade `builtin:tr-audio-cross-fade`); pass one as `assetId`. If the seam already has a transition of the same kind (visual vs audio), this replaces/updates that transition instead of duplicating it; existing duration is preserved unless `durationInFrames` is explicitly passed. Pass `replaceExisting:false` only when you want duplicate detection to error.
- **`targetItemId` / `outgoingItemId` / `incomingItemId` must reference existing items**. To add a new item AND attach an effect/transition to it, use two calls (add the item, `preview_timeline` for the new id, then add the effect/transition).

# Ripple

`ripple:true` is timeline-movement mode: adds push later items forward; deletes close gaps. Use it when the requested edit is naturally an insertion, gap close, or sequence rewrite; do not use it merely because an overlap happened.

# Examples

- **Dry-run**: pass `validateOnly:true` with the same `adds` / `updates` / `deletes` you plan to commit.
- **Swap B-roll**: `deletes:[{id:"old"}]`, `adds:[{type:"video",assetId:"new",fromFrame:120,durationInFrames:60,trackId:"V1"}]`
- **Add 30s at timeline 5s without moving existing items**: `adds:[{type:"video",assetId:"...",from:"5s",duration:"30s"}]` (omit `trackId` so auto-placement can choose a non-overlapping track)
- **Splice 4 videos on V1**: `adds:[{...,"alignTo":"track-end"}, {...,"alignTo":"track-end"}, ...]` (chained)
- **Rebuild a track**: list every existing item id in `deletes` and the new layout in `adds` — atomic, no overlap.

# Desktop AI Portrait Cutout

- Apply background removal with `{type:"effect",assetId:"builtin:effect-ai-portrait-matte",targetItemId:"<image or video item id>"}`.
- It is available on ChatCut Desktop for macOS, Windows, and Linux. The target must be one image or video clip. Do not pass GIF targets, trackId, fromFrame, durationInFrames, or track-bound range fields.
- Optional `propertyOverrides`: `edgeFeather` (0–100), `matteOffset` (-50–50), `outlineStyle` (`"none"`, `"solid"`, or `"dashed"`), `outlineColor`, `outlineWidth` (1–20), and `outlinePlacement` (-50–50). For dashed outlines, use `outlineDashLength` (1–100), `outlineDashGap` (0–100), and `outlineDashOffset` (-100–100). Desktop downloads the model and prepares the matte cache automatically.

# Desktop Linear Mask

Apply assetId:"builtin:effect-linear-mask" using the effect shapes above. Linear alpha mask: use propertyOverrides = {direction:180,stops:[{position:0,opacity:1},{position:0.25,opacity:1},{position:1,opacity:0}]}. Flux renders this native built-in effect. Direction is 0–360 degrees: 0 bottom-to-top, 90 left-to-right, 180 top-to-bottom, 270 right-to-left. Reverse the direction by adding 180 modulo 360, keeping stops unchanged. Stop positions and opacity are 0–1; provide 2–8 stops. Opacity 1 keeps the source visible, 0 reveals layers below. Stops interpolate linearly in position order; equal positions create a hard edge. Missing endpoints interpolate toward opacity 1 at position 0 and opacity 0 at position 1. For existing masks, including track-bound masks, use edit_item updates:[{type:"effect",id:"<effect item id>",propertyOverrides:{direction:<degrees>,stops:<complete stops array>}}]. Send the complete propertyOverrides when editing to preserve both direction and stops. Set direction:180 explicitly for the top-to-bottom fade in the example.

adds.description: Regular item/effect/transition adds. Prefer this over json. Inside each entry, fadeIn/fadeOut/audioFadeIn/audioFadeOut are seconds, not frames. For a 60-frame fade at 30fps, pass audioFadeOut:2 or audioFadeOutDurationInFrames:60; never pass audioFadeOut:60 to mean 60 frames.

deletes.description: Items/effects/transitions to delete, as objects: [{id:"item id"}]. Prefer this over json.

id.description: Existing item/effect/transition id or prefix to delete.

json.description: Legacy compatibility: a JSON object string containing adds/updates/deletes. Prefer passing adds/updates/deletes directly instead of using this string wrapper.

projectId.description: Existing project ID from the editor URL or list_projects. Pass this when continuing work on an existing project and the external MCP session is not already targeted.

ripple.description: Timeline-movement mode. Use when the edit intent is insertion/make-room/shift-later-items/close-gap/sequence-rewrite.

updates.description: Existing item/effect/transition updates. Prefer this over json. Inside each entry, fadeIn/fadeOut/audioFadeIn/audioFadeOut are seconds, not frames. For a 60-frame fade at 30fps, pass audioFadeOut:2 or audioFadeOutDurationInFrames:60; never pass audioFadeOut:60 to mean 60 frames.

validateOnly.description: Dry-run validation/planning without committing timeline changes. Do not combine with ripple.
